diagnosis: Anatomical and functional imaging in a patient with an abdominal paraganglioma
legend: The patient was a 13-year-old girl in a family with a known SDHB mutation. Two older family members had already developed paragangliomas. Genetic testing confirmed that she was also a mutation carrier. Biochemical testing for metanephrines was negative. CT (shown here) and whole-body MIBG scan showed a small midline paraganglioma with varied histological patterns.

diagnosis: Anatomical and functional imaging in a patient with an abdominal paraganglioma
legend: The patient was a 13-year-old girl in a family with a known SDHB mutation. Two older family members had already developed paragangliomas. Genetic testing confirmed that she was also a mutation carrier. Biochemical testing for metanephrines was negative. CT and whole-body MIBG scan showed a small midline paraganglioma with varied histological patterns, including irregular nests and cords of cells with prominent intervening sclerosis (shown here). Intratumoural heterogeneity was also observed with respect to several immunohistochemical markers.

diagnosis: Biomarker expression in an abdominal paraganglioma
legend: Staining of a resected paraganglioma for SSTR2A can be useful as a preliminary test to assess whether functional imaging or treatment with radiolabelled somatostatin analogues would be suitable to screen for or treat metastases. Most sympathetic paragangliomas express SSTR2A; however, intratumoural heterogeneity can be marked, like in this example.

diagnosis: Biomarker expression in an abdominal paraganglioma
legend: Sympathetic paragangliomas can show intratumoural heterogeneity with respect to biomarker expression. Transcription factors are often diffusely expressed, whereas expression of functional markers can be focal and weak. Shown here is a uniformly positive immunohistochemical stain for GATA3, showing characteristic nuclear staining in paraganglioma and in two neurons in an adjacent normal ganglion at the bottom.

diagnosis: Biomarker expression in an abdominal paraganglioma
legend: Highly variable staining for tyrosine hydroxylase.

A paraganglioma from a patient with a hereditary SDHB mutation, who was screened for tumours in her early twenties. At that time, she had already developed three paragangliomas (34–47 mm) adjacent to her lumbar vertebrae, each with a somewhat different gross appearance.
source: Dr. Harry Kozakewich, Boston Childrens Hospital

legend: Multiple histological patterns can be found in synchronous paragangliomas with the same genetic background. This solid growth pattern with a high cellularity was associated with tumour necrosis and coarse nodularity (not shown); all of these are putative risk factors for metastasis.
source: Dr. Harry Kozakewich, Boston Childrens Hospital
